display.purpose: The single hero H1, capped at 16ch so it always breaks into masked lines.

claim.purpose: The closing 'Marque seu horário.' over the footer facade band.

headline.purpose: Section H2s in Craft, Menu and Barbers.

statement.purpose: Editorial copy promoted to display scale: the manifesto paragraph and the Trust blockquote.

subhead.purpose: The gallery H2, deliberately the quietest section title.

title.purpose: Service names and prices (1.5→2rem), barber names (1.6rem), mobile menu links (2rem).

title-sm.purpose: Footer column heads; the header wordmark sits just above at 1.4rem.

body.purpose: Leads and paragraphs, capped 38–52ch; 1.1rem in the hero at sm, 0.98rem in footer data.

body-sm.purpose: Button labels on the solid and outline WhatsApp variants.

label.purpose: Barber notes (0.92), header nav (0.9), Google badge and map link (0.88), small CTAs and notes (0.85).

micro.purpose: Hero meta, service durations, the quiet booking link, footer closing line (0.82); gallery captions at 0.78 are the floor.

shadows.name: overlap-cast
shadows.purpose: Desktop-only cast under the Craft section's overlapping second figure; reads as contact between layers, not a container.

shadows.name: floating-action-ambient
shadows.purpose: Lifts the mobile-only circular WhatsApp control above scrolling content.

motion.name: mq-desktop
motion.purpose: Gate for every scrubbed transform, parallax, pin and Lenis smooth scroll.

motion.name: mq-touch
motion.value: (max-width: 1023px) or ((min-width: 1024px) and (pointer: coarse)), both with prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
motion.purpose: One-shot reveals only: no pin, no scrub, no smooth-scroll hijack.

motion.name: ease-entrance
motion.purpose: Default easing for reveals and entrance tweens.

motion.name: ease-wipe
motion.purpose: clip-path inset() wipes on figures and the Trust hairline.

motion.name: ease-scrub
motion.purpose: Every scroll-linked tween is linear; the scroll supplies the curve.

motion.name: ease-ui
motion.purpose: CSS-driven hover, focus and reveal transitions: the bordô colour layer (420ms), underline wipes (380ms), image scale settles (700–900ms).

motion.name: reveal-lines
motion.value: SplitText.create({ type: 'lines', mask: 'lines', linesClass: 'reveal-line', autoSplit: true }) → gsap.from(lines, { yPercent: 108, duration: 1.05, stagger: 0.085, ease: power3.out })
motion.purpose: Signature masked line-by-line heading reveal; .reveal-line carries padding-bottom 0.14em / margin-bottom -0.14em so serif descenders are not clipped.

motion.name: lenis-smooth-scroll
motion.value: new Lenis({ duration: 1.05, smoothWheel: true, syncTouch: false, touchMultiplier: 1 }) bridged to ScrollTrigger.update via gsap.ticker
motion.purpose: Desktop pointer only; on touch the scroll stays 100% native.

motion.name: gallery-pin
motion.value: ScrollTrigger { pin: true, scrub: 1, end: () => `+=${track.scrollWidth - innerWidth + 96}`, invalidateOnRefresh: true, anticipatePin: 1 }
motion.purpose: The single pinned stage in the system: the gallery strip translating horizontally, desktop only.

motion.name: reduced-motion-guard
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce → no matchMedia context runs; base layer flattens animation/transition to 0.01ms
motion.purpose: Nothing moves and nothing hides: every tween is gsap.from() off a naturally visible CSS state. Audit: zero elements render below 0.15 opacity.

narrative.overview: Gireh's site reads like a bespoke suit's fitting room, not a barbershop marquee: a dark, tonal room built from two near-blacks (carvão and grafite), one warm brushed-metal accent (latão) spent sparingly, and a deep wine (bordô) that only ever arrives as a moving surface behind a label. The system refuses the generic "preto e dourado" barbershop-luxury cliché and vintage-Americana barber-pole tropes — no high-gloss gold, no pole motif, no ornamental flourish. Precision carries the premium signal: square corners everywhere, a single engraved-plate serif reserved for names and headlines, and photography that sits naked in the composition rather than inside a frame. The rebuilt site is editorial and large-format. The type ramp runs from 0.78rem captions to a 6.5rem hero in fluid clamp() steps, so the display voice actually dominates its viewport instead of politely fitting. Compositions bleed past the container and overlap on purpose — the manifesto figure runs off the right edge, the craft scene stacks two absolutely positioned figures, the gallery is a horizontal strip of mismatched widths. There are no cards: no bordered boxes around images, no shadowed containers, no padded tiles. Depth comes from tonal layering, gradient veils and overlap. Motion is now central rather than rationed, and it is deliberately platform-split. Desktop with a mouse gets Lenis smooth wheel scrolling bridged into GSAP ScrollTrigger: parallax at different speeds per layer, scale drift, and exactly one pinned horizontal section. Touch gets native scroll and one-shot reveals only — no pinning, no scrubbed transforms, no scroll hijacking. Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves and, critically, nothing hides: every animation is authored as gsap.from() off a naturally visible CSS state.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, tonal "atelier room" of two near-black surfaces (carvão, grafite) alternating section to section; depth from layering and overlap, never from card chrome.
One warm accent (latão) as text-safe accent and interactive signal; bordô as a non-text colour layer that animates in from the bottom.
A dramatic fluid serif ramp topping out at 6.5rem, against a precise grotesk for every functional line.
No cards, no image frames, no borders around photography — hairlines rule lists and edges only.
A platform-split motion system: scrubbed parallax and one pin on desktop pointers; one-shot reveals on touch; nothing hidden under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Latão Rule
rules.body: Latão is a text colour only on carvão or grafite. It never appears as text on osso or any light surface — measured contrast there (2.50:1) fails AA, against 5.83:1 on carvão and 5.18:1 on grafite. Binding, from PRODUCT.md's accessibility contract.

rules.name: The Non-Text Bordô Rule
rules.body: Bordô is never a text colour, full stop; it exists only as fill, border, or the hover/focus colour layer. Its ~1.3–1.4:1 contrast against the dark surfaces makes any bordô text unreadable and unshippable. Binding, from PRODUCT.md's accessibility contract.

rules.name: The Opacity-Not-Grey Rule
rules.body: Secondary and tertiary text is osso at reduced alpha, never a new neutral. The palette stays at six colours no matter how many tiers of copy a section needs.

rules.name: The Names-Get-the-Serif Rule
rules.body: The display serif is reserved for headlines, statements, barber names and prices — anything that reads like it belongs on an engraved plate. Body copy, labels, buttons, nav and all UI chrome stay in Archivo; the two never trade places.

rules.name: The Descender-Clearance Rule
rules.body: Any heading revealed line-by-line through a mask carries the .reveal-line padding/margin pair (padding-bottom: 0.14em; margin-bottom: -0.14em). Without it the serif's g, j and p are clipped by the mask's overflow. Every masked reveal inherits this class from revealLines(); never mask a serif line without it.

rules.name: The Fluid-Only Rule
rules.body: Every step above 1.35rem is a clamp(), not a breakpoint stack. The ramp scales continuously with the viewport; new display-scale type states its own clamp rather than stepping through sm:/lg: sizes.

rules.name: The No-Card Rule
rules.body: This system has no cards. Images are placed bare into the composition — no border, no radius, no padded container, no surface tint behind them. If a group of content needs definition, it gets a hairline rule, a tonal band, or nothing.

rules.name: The Two-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Exactly two shadows exist site-wide: one under the overlapping craft figure and one under the floating action button. Sections, lists, images and interactive surfaces are shadowless.

rules.name: The Platform-Split Motion Rule
rules.body: Desktop and touch are different platforms, not the same site at different widths. Scroll-scrubbed transforms, parallax, pinning and smooth-scroll are gated behind (min-width: 1024px) and (pointer: fine) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Touch gets native scroll plus one-shot reveals, and nothing else. A coarse pointer at 1400px gets the touch treatment, not the desktop one.

rules.name: The Nothing-Hidden Rule
rules.body: Every animation is authored as gsap.from() off a state that is already visible in CSS. Reduced motion, a failed script, or a media query that never matches must all leave the page fully readable. Audit test: with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, no element renders below 0.15 opacity.

rules.name: The One-Pin Rule
rules.body: The gallery is the only pinned section in the system, and only on desktop pointers. A second pin, or any pin on touch, is out of system.

dos: Do keep latão as a text colour only on carvão or grafite — never on osso or any light surface.
Do express the bordô microinteraction as a colour layer scaling from origin-bottom under the label, on hover and :focus-visible, so keyboard users get the same state as mouse users.
Do place photography bare into the composition and let it bleed, overlap, or run off the gutter; use carvão gradient veils, not borders, to control legibility over it.
Do gate every scrubbed, parallaxed or pinned effect behind the desktop media query, and give touch a one-shot reveal instead.
Do author reveals as gsap.from() and attach .reveal-line to any masked serif heading so descenders clear the mask.
Do alternate carvão and grafite bands to separate sections, and rule lists with bronze hairlines at 25–40% opacity.
donts: Don't use bordô as a text colour under any circumstance; it is fill, border and hover layer only.
Don't introduce cards: no bordered boxes, no rounded containers, no shadowed tiles, no frames around images.
Don't add a third shadow. The craft overlap cast and the floating action button's ambient are the complete vocabulary.
Don't round corners. The system is square; the circular floating action button is the sole, purposeful exception.
Don't add a second pinned section, run scrubbed transforms on touch, or let Lenis take over scrolling on a coarse pointer.
Don't invent a new neutral for secondary copy — step osso down by opacity instead.
Don't reach for "preto e dourado" generic luxury signalling, high-gloss gold, or vintage barber-pole imagery.
